subject: Confirmation: Customer data not used for model improvement — logging & retention next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Green <alyssa.green@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up & commitments from today's demo — data handling summary

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation with your data governance and apps teams. Per our discussion I wanted to summarize the commitments Redwood is prepared to make for Meridian Health as part of the DL-2026-0897 evaluation: 

- Training-on-customer-data: Redwood will not use your customer content (any PII or PHI) for model training, tuning, or evaluation unless you explicitly opt in in writing. This covers both supervised retraining and any offline fine-tuning pipelines.
- Logging controls and retention: We will provide configurable access/logging retention windows. Default is 30 days for request/response logs but we can extend to 90 days under an enterprise configuration with contractual terms.
- PII handling: We support automated redaction/masking at ingestion and recommend tokenization for fields that might contain PHI.
- Data residency: Production inference and audit logs can be pinned to a US region (us-west-2) to meet your residency constraints.
- Key management & encryption: Customer-managed KMS is available for encryption at rest; network traffic is TLS 1.3.

I attached a short operational statement (PDF) you can share with procurement/security as a starting point. Next steps I propose:
1) Procurement/security review the attached statement and confirm any additions.
2) We schedule a 30-minute session with one of our security engineers (Neha) to cover SOC2 evidence and the logging/retention controls in detail.
3) If you want a written amendment for the trial, I can pull in legal after we finalize the exact retention window.

Please let me know if I missed anything.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thank you for the clear recap. Meridian is comfortable with the high-level commitments you listed but procurement/security need a formal confirmation for two items before we can move to PO: 

1) Explicit statement that no customer data will be used for model improvement (no exceptions unless opt-in). We need wording we can attach to the SOW.
2) Confirmation of log retention behavior and what gets scrubbed: request/response payloads, access logs, and system-level diagnostics. We prefer a 90-day retention for access/audit logs.

Also attached are our SOC2 checklist questions — could Neha or someone from security answer rows 7–10 about key rotation and retention?

If you can provide the formal statement and a brief answersheet for the SOC2 rows, I can circulate to our legal and get procurement to prepare the PO.

Best,
Alyssa Green
Director, IT Security Operations
Meridian Health

Subject: Re: Follow-up & commitments from today's demo — data handling summary

Alyssa —

Appreciate the quick reply and the SOC2 matrix. Attached is a short formal statement you can append to the SOW: it explicitly states that Redwood will not leverage Meridian customer data for model training or improvement unless Meridian provides express written consent. It also lists the configurable logging retention tiers (30 / 90 / custom contract).

Quick answers to your SOC2 rows 7–10:
- Key management: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS) and can provide key rotation logs on request.
- Key rotation: Rotation is configurable; default rotation policy is 365 days. We provide rotation audit events in the audit log.
- Retention: Access and audit logs are retained based on the contracted window; request/response payloads can be configured to never be persisted beyond the retention window and can be scrubbed on ingest.
- Diagnostics data: System diagnostics are separated from user payloads and do not contain PII by default; we can provide a redaction profile to ensure stripping of identifiers.

Next step: Neha — can we confirm the 90-day retention option in writing and provide the redaction profile? If so I'll route the statement to Meridian procurement.

Thanks,
Alex

Hi Alyssa —

Following up with the operational confirmations you requested. Short answers below; happy to expand in the security session.

1) Training-on-customer-data: Confirmed — Redwood will not use Meridian customer data (including PII/PHI) for any model improvement, evaluation, or augmentation pipelines unless you provide explicit, recorded consent. This is an enforceable contractual control we can include in the SOW.

2) Retention & scrubbing: We support three configurable behaviors for request payloads: (a) never persist (stateless), (b) persist encrypted for X days then purge, (c) persist with automatic field-level redaction. For access/audit logs we will enable a 90-day retention window per request. System diagnostics are collected in a separate channel and are scrubbed to remove identifiers by default.

3) Logging destination & residency: Logs and audit trails can be stored in your chosen US region (us-west-2). If you require the storage account (S3) to be in a customer-owned bucket, we can support that via cross-account roles.

4) KMS & rotation: Customer-managed KMS supported; rotation events emitted to audit logs. We can provide rotation proof for compliance review.

5) Proof & evidence: We will provide a short evidence bundle for procurement containing: the statement (attached by Alex), sample redaction profile, and a link to our SOC2 evidence portal for read-only access during procurement review.

If the above aligns, Alex — please share the attached statement with procurement and I will prepare the short evidence bundle and carve out 30 minutes for a technical Q&A with Alyssa's team.

-Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Engineering
Redwood Inference
